tagline: South over the last of the tallgrass, radio on.
intro: K-177 leaves Council Grove, whose Main Street is the old Santa Fe Trail, and runs south over the Flint Hills to Cassoday, crossing creek after creek and keeping company with the railroad much of the way. North of Strong City it passes through Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve. Less than five percent of the tallgrass prairie that once covered the continent remains, most of it in these hills.
Tune the radio to 1680 AM. Transmitters at Council Grove, Cottonwood Falls and Cassoday tell of ranching and prairie wildlife, and why ranchers burn their pastures.

moments.title: Council Grove
moments.text: Named for an 1827 treaty with the Osage signed under an oak, the town later used a tree as its post office, where travelers left mail for whoever was going the right way.

moments.title: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
moments.text: Stephen Jones built his Second Empire ranch house here in 1881, early in the fencing of the open range, and since 2009 the preserve has kept a bison herd.

moments.title: Cottonwood Falls
moments.text: The Chase County Courthouse, of local limestone with a three-story winding staircase of local walnut, has been at work since 1873, longer than any other in Kansas.
